items.title: The best way to run Docker on Proxmox depends entirely on your hardware and use-case, and it took me years to realize that
items.author: Ayush Pande
items.content: Although Proxmox ships with terrific virtualization and LXC management tools, there are certain projects that may require a Docker instance. Perhaps you’re new to Proxmox Virtual Environment and want a familiar method for spinning up free and open-source tools in containers. Or maybe you’re looking to deploy an obscure service that doesn’t have dedicated LXC packages or fails to install as an OCI-based container on Proxmox.

items.title: Google Assistant is dead, and I won't miss it thanks to my local LLM
items.author: Nolen Jonker
items.content: Voice assistants have been part of the phone experience for so long that most of us don't really give them second thought anymore. Google is now pulling the plug on the biggest one though. Google Assistant is going away on September 4, 2026, and there's no toggle back to it once your phone flips over.

items.title: Someone built a 3D cyberpunk city entirely from ASCII characters, and it's shockingly impressive
items.author: Patrick O'Rourke
items.content: As far as ASCII art goes, this is one of the most impressive projects I've ever seen.

items.title: 6 Google Pixel features I disabled to dramatically improve battery life
items.author: Parth Shah
items.content: Pixel phones have never been battery champions for me, but I had mostly learned to live with it. I blamed the usual suspects without realizing that some of Google’s own features were quietly adding to the drain. Once I started digging through their settings and disabled a few things I barely used, the difference was noticeable almost immediately.

items.title: I tested Obsidian Bases against Notion with a real project, and one of them fell apart
items.author: Nolen Jonker
items.content: Every Notion account has a graveyard of abandoned databases. Databases themselves aren't even that hard to navigate, but they can get tedious under constant maintenance, which is part of the reason I left Notion a while ago in favor of simpler, more minimalist options. One of them is Obsidian's Bases plugin, which finally enabled many to leave Notion behind.

items.title: 4 self-hosted alternatives to apps you're still paying for every month
items.author: Patrick Hearn
items.content: Every time I turn around, it seems like something else has gone up in price. Netflix seems to have embarked on a quest to make streaming as unaffordable as cable, and even my garbage company emails me every few months about raising rates. One part of my life that doesn't have to suffer from increased prices is software, though. While there are plenty of services I am more than happy to pay for (and no more than a few minutes of your time.

items.title: These Pixel features seemed overhyped until I tried them for the first time
items.author: Megan Ellis
items.content: There are plenty of Pixel-exclusive features, but I haven't been able to experience them until now. The reason? Pixel devices aren't available where I live, so the brand is something you hear about in headlines, but not something many people have hands-on experience with locally.

items.title: I stopped running every Docker container 24/7, and my home server has never been better
items.author: Yash Patel
items.content: Self-hosting has always been about controlling the software I use. Docker made that even easier. I could try a new application, deploy it in minutes, and keep adding more services to my server. That flexibility is one reason I enjoy running my own infrastructure.

items.title: I use these Docker containers to manage my entire digital life
items.author: Parth Shah
items.content: Docker started as a way for me to experiment with a few self-hosted apps, but it quickly turned into a crucial part of my digital life. Now, everything from my personal cloud storage to my project manager runs in its own isolated container and gives me unparalleled control, privacy, and flexibility. Let me walk you through my entire setup and show you how I use these Docker containers to manage my entire digital life.

items.title: GIMP 3.3.2 will change the default project file format for the first time in almost 30 years
items.author: Simon Batt
items.content: GIMP has gone from strength to strength in recent months. Back in March, we saw the introduction of non-destructive Link Layers that didn't lose fidelity no matter how much you squashed and stretched them. Now, the team has revealed that it's digging into the default project file format introduced in 1997 to give GIMP a more modern feel.
